chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, he said:
I asked him about the ground and the rooftop that urine or something similar comes upon: does the sun purify it without water? He said: “How can it be purified without water?”

What is meant by it is when the sun has not dried it. What indicates that is the first report, which is his statement: “If impurity comes upon the ground and the sun rises over it, then it dries, there is no harm in praying upon it; but if it has not dried, then prayer upon it is not permissible.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: There is no harm in a person praying on bedding that semen or some other impurity has affected, so long as the place of his sajdah is pure. This is indicated by it.

key_terms.السَّطْحِ: the rooftop or elevated surface affected by impurity
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose drying effect is central to the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), whose validity on such surfaces is being addressed
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the ground or earth as a surface discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, a source of najasah mentioned in the report
key_terms.سُجُودِهِ: his sajdah, meaning the place of prostration that must be pure
key_terms.طَاهِرًا: pure, describing the required state of the place of prostration

ai.seo_question: Does the sun purify ground or surfaces affected by najasah for salat without water?
ai.summary: This text discusses the ruling on impurity affecting the ground or surfaces and whether the sun purifies them. It indicates that mere sunlight without the relevant drying effect does not suffice, while a dried surface may be suitable for salat. It also states that prayer on bedding affected by impurity is acceptable if the place of sajdah is pure.
